position.name: Adolescent Mental Health Technician

streetAddress.location: 4900 S University Dr, Davie, FL 33328, USA

position.description:
Adolescent Mental Health Technician (Bilingual: English & Spanish)

On Site | Davie, FL | Part-Time | 3p-8p, Monday-Friday  | Bilingual

Compensation: This role starts at $17.00/hour during the onboarding and training period. After successful completion of training and certification in core responsibilities, pay increases to $19.00/hour.

About the Role

Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) is hiring for our adolescent PHP (Partial Hospitalization Program) and IOP (Intensive Outpatient Program) in Davie, FL. Both full-time and part-time schedules are open, and bilingual Spanish is required for the part time role.

You are the operational backbone of the AWA program environment. You ensure the day-to-day experience for adolescent clients is safe, structured, and therapeutically consistent — from the moment they arrive to the moment they leave. This role is hands-on, fast-paced, and client-facing, requiring calm under pressure and genuine investment in the teens you serve.

Backgrounds that translate well: Direct Care · Youth Counselor · Residential Counselor · Mental Health Technician · Psych Tech · Paraprofessional · Behavior Technician · Group Home · Youth Care Worker · Case Aide · Education · Community Services

What You'll Do

  • Supervise adolescent clients ages 13–17 during groups, sessions, transitions, breaks, and unstructured milieu time
  • Monitor and maintain program safety; respond to escalated behavior using trauma-informed care and crisis intervention protocols
  • De-escalate conflict and redirect behavior without power struggles
  • Support therapists and clinicians in maintaining therapeutic schedules and daily program flow
  • Greet and assist families at drop-off and pick-up with professionalism and warmth, in English and Spanish
  • Manage front desk responsibilities including phones, attendance, and client sign-in/sign-out
  • Complete accurate, same-day EMR documentation including wellness check-ins, behavioral observations, and incident reports
  • Escalate safety concerns, disclosures, and behavioral flags to the clinical team immediately and appropriately
  • Support program operations with light administrative and organizational tasks

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 1–2 years of adolescent experience in a school, clinical, behavioral health, camp, residential, or community setting
  • Demonstrated ability to de-escalate, regulate, and maintain structure without power struggles
  • Strong documentation and incident reporting skills
  • Emotionally regulated, professional, and consistent under pressure
  • Understands the limits of a non-clinical role — escalates appropriately, never makes independent clinical decisions
  • Bilingual: fluent Spanish and English
  • Must pass a Level 2 background screening and pre-employment drug screen
  • Reliable transportation to our Davie, FL location

Preferred

  • Bachelor's degree in psychology, social work, human services, education, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience considered
  • CPI, MANDT, or NCI crisis prevention training
  • Prior experience in an outpatient or residential mental health setting
  • Familiarity with EMR/EHR documentation

AWA is an adolescent mental health organization operating PHP and IOP programs in South Florida. We exist to serve teens and families at their most critical moments — and this role is at the center of that work every day.

Learn More: Adolescent Wellness Academy

I am writing to express my interest in the Wellness Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. Working closely with teachers and students strengthened my ability to foster trust, encourage emotional regulation, and support positive student development. 

What draws me most to Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to combine my passion for psychology, youth support, and wellness advocacy in a meaningful school-based role. Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to further discuss how my experience and skills align with the goals of Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,
Roen Cooney

Served in a lead supervisory role providing direct care, structure, guidance, and around-the-clock supervision to adolescents within a secure juvenile detention and residential treatment environment. Supervised Youth Specialists and helped coordinate daily shift operations, staff assignments, youth movement, security procedures, and program activities while ensuring compliance with facility policies and Florida Department of Juvenile Justice standards.

Monitored residents’ behavior, emotional well-being, peer interactions, and compliance with individualized treatment and behavioral plans. Used trauma-informed care, positive reinforcement, redirection, conflict resolution, crisis intervention, and verbal de-escalation techniques to help youth manage anger, impulsivity, trauma responses, behavioral challenges, and mental-health concerns.

Maintained confidentiality, professional boundaries, and a fair, consistent, and respectful approach when working with adolescents from diverse backgrounds.

This position strengthened my leadership abilities and gave me extensive experience supporting adolescents affected by trauma, family instability, mental-health conditions, behavioral concerns, substance use, and involvement in the juvenile justice system.

I left the position to pursue continued professional growth and an opportunity more closely focused on adolescent mental-health treatment, emotional wellness, and rehabilitation. My experience in juvenile detention gave me a strong foundation in youth supervision, leadership, crisis intervention, trauma-informed care, behavioral management, documentation, safety, and relationship building. I am now looking to apply those skills in a therapeutic environment where I can continue helping adolescents develop healthier coping skills, make positive choices, and work toward long-term stability and success.

Good afternoon,

I am a dedicated and compassionate social services professional with over eight years of experience supporting children, adolescents, and families. My experience in child welfare, youth diversion, and behavioral health has developed my ability to build rapport with youth, manage challenging situations, communicate effectively, and maintain a safe and supportive environment. I am passionate about helping adolescents feel heard, respected, and supported while encouraging positive behaviors and healthy decision-making.

As a Child Protective Investigator with the Florida Department of Children and Families, I worked directly with children and adolescents experiencing a variety of behavioral, emotional, and family-related challenges. I conducted interviews, assessed safety and well-being, collaborated with parents, schools, medical professionals, law enforcement, and community providers, maintained confidential documentation, and connected families with counseling and other behavioral health resources. This experience strengthened my ability to recognize concerns, respond appropriately to difficult situations, and work effectively with a multidisciplinary team.

Previously, as a Youth Diversion Counselor with the Broward Sheriff's Office, I worked closely with adolescents to address behavioral and social risk factors, reduce recidivism, strengthen family relationships, and connect youth with educational and behavioral health resources. I encouraged positive decision-making and helped youth develop stronger connections to their families and communities. Additionally, my experience at Fifth Street Counseling Center provided exposure to a behavioral health setting, where I supported clients, maintained records, conducted random drug testing, and assisted with daily operations.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

     I am excited to apply for a position with your adolescent wellness team. With a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, current graduate studies in Human Services with a focus on Crisis Resiliency, and professional experience supporting children, adolescents, and families, I am passionate about helping young people navigate challenges and develop the tools they need to thrive.
For the past several years, I have served as a Youth Director, where I have had the opportunity to lead and mentor middle and high school students. In this role, I build meaningful relationships with adolescents, provide emotional and spiritual support, respond to concerns and difficult situations, collaborate with parents and leadership, and create programs that promote healthy development, connection, and resilience. This experience has taught me the importance of meeting young people where they are, listening without judgment, and creating an environment where they feel safe, valued, and heard.
      My experience as a Registered Behavior Technician has further strengthened my ability to work with youth in a behavioral health setting. I have experience implementing individualized treatment plans, documenting client progress, collecting behavioral data, managing challenging behaviors, and collaborating with families and clinical supervisors. These experiences have developed my patience, communication skills, attention to detail, and ability to remain calm and compassionate in challenging situations.
      I am particularly drawn to adolescent wellness because I believe early support can make a lasting difference in a young person's life. My professional and academic experiences have strengthened my desire to work at the intersection of mental health, crisis resiliency, and youth development. I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my experience, passion for adolescents, and commitment to compassionate care to your organization.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and passion for working with youth could contribute to your team.
Sincerely,
Genesis Medina

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the adolescent mental health technician position in your organization. I recently graduated from Florida Atlantic University with a bachelors in psychology, and I am currently taking a gap year to gain meaningful research and professional experience before continuing my education. My primary research interests include interbrain synchrony, human development, developmental psychology, and social behavior. 

My academic background has provided me with a strong foundation in human development, developmental psychology, and social behavior. At Florida Atlantic University, I completed projects focused on understanding how individuals behave and interact with others. One project involved designing and conducting a behavioral observational study examining factors that influenced whether individuals approached a table on a university campus. I collected and analyzed behavioral data and worked with classmates to identify and interpret behavioral patterns. I also analyzed peer-reviewed research on interbrain synchrony and social neuroscience, evaluating research methods and findings related to social interaction and human behavior. These experiences strengthened my ability to carefully observe behavior, recognize patterns, communicate effectively, and approach individual behavior with curiosity and without judgment.

I am especially interested in this position because it would allow me to work directly with adolescents while applying my psychology background in a meaningful setting. I understand that working with adolescents in a mental health environment requires patience, empathy, professionalism, strong communication, and the ability to remain calm and attentive in challenging situations. I am eager to support patients in their daily routines, contribute to a safe and positive environment, and learn from professionals who work closely with adolescents experiencing mental health challenges. 

Thank you for considering my application. I am eager to bring my psychology background, strong communication skills, and genuine interest in helping others to this position. I would appreciate the opportunity to work alongside your team, support adolescents in their treatment, and contribute to a safe and encouraging environment. I am confident that this experience would allow me to make a meaningful contribution while continuing to develop my skills and knowledge in the mental health field. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how I could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Emily Kogan

Andrea Malo 
305-606-0671

7 August 2026

Dear Hiring Manager: 
I am reaching out regarding the Adolescent Mental Health Technician position at your facility, Adolescent Wellness Academy. Given my Bachelor of Science degree in psychology and my experience working with preschool to adolescent age groups, I believe that this is a great prospect for what I am hoping to pursue as a long-term career. 
As mentioned, I received a bachelor’s degree in psychology as well as having been working with the preschool to adolescent age groups for nearly five years. These jobs have ranged from camp counsellor, after-school enrichment program teacher, child shadow, and teacher assistant. With the younger population, I have encountered children that have had a range of behavioral issues and intellectual disabilities; this includes anger management issues, Autism Spectrum Disorder, ADHD, and more. In the adolescent age group, there has been much similarity to the younger group but with the additional concerns of bullying, emotional distress, among other concerns. While working with those with ADHD and behavioral disruptions, there were ways where I learned to cater more to what the child would best respond to while de-escalating the behavior. Thus, at times the procedure was to distract the child before their energy was exerted in a negative/aggressive way by giving them jobs to complete in the class; other times it was to remove them from the situation as soon as possible. 
Another program I have worked on is the Crisis Prevention Line. Recently, I received my certification needed to engage with the program and have been volunteering for nearly six months. The certification needed for the program required me to solidify my skills in de-escalating intense situations as well as engaging with the person in a natural and helpful way rather than interrogative. In the program, I encountered users who have come in with substance abuse concerns, relationship concerns, social anxiety, paranoia, and more like. These moments have challenged me to be more cognizant of my words given the heightened risk for prevention. Each situation has been different, but it has allowed me to see the different responses to help that people present. While some have been grateful for my help, others have, admittingly, not been as responsive. Given that I am relatively new to the program, I am constantly communicating with my advisor in case of an emergency in order to know how to best respond to the given situation, making sure to keep them updated on the newest changes/information. Doing this work has brought me closer to solidifying the course I wish to take in my specialization regarding crisis prevention. 
Upon looking at this opportunity I found that it aligned with exactly what I am seeking for in a job in the community. As your program is centered around PHP and IOP work, I am interested in providing my help in this department. I like how IOP's provide patients the freedom as well as help needed for their recovery. Using these methods provides the structure that these adolescents may need in a more approachable way. It is a technique that encourages personalization to treatment processes rather than focusing on a general approach, which does not work for every individual. Since I am certified with the Volunteer Crisis Counseling Training -- given that I volunteer with the Crisis Prevention Line -- in crisis prevention and de-escalation skills, I am ready to apply these procedures in a physical environment rather than only through media. I believe these responsibilities will strengthen my desire to continue pursuing this career path as I will be able to make a meaningful change both in the people I am assisting as well as myself. 
Once again, I look forward to this opportunity. I appreciate your consideration of me for a possible position, and I look forward to hearing back in any way. Thank you once more.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Adolescent Mental Health Technician position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a social work professional with experience supporting adolescents in youth development, mental health, and child welfare settings, I am passionate about creating safe, structured, and supportive environments where young people can develop emotionally and socially. I am currently pursuing my Master of Social Work at Florida Atlantic University and hold a Bachelor of Social Work from Florida Memorial University. My academic background and hands-on experience have strengthened my ability to connect with adolescents while maintaining professionalism, structure, and consistency in challenging situations.

My previous experience has prepared me well for the hands-on responsibilities of this position. As a Youth Counselor with First Star University of Miami Academy, I supported adolescents through academic assistance, life-skills activities, daily supervision, and relationship building. I supervised students during daily activities, meals, and dormitory routines while promoting safety, accountability, and positive behavior. Additionally, as a Wellness Intern with Guitars Over Guns, I conducted individual support sessions, facilitated groups for middle and high school students, provided emotional support, and responded to behavioral outbursts through intervention and de-escalation. I also completed documentation, utilized the Children’s Global Assessment Scale (CGAS), and collaborated in developing individualized, goal-oriented service plans. These experiences have taught me the importance of remaining calm under pressure, establishing appropriate boundaries, recognizing behavioral concerns, and creating an environment where adolescents feel supported and respected.

I am particularly interested in AWA because of its focus on adolescent mental health and its commitment to providing a structured therapeutic environment. My experience with strengths-based engagement, social-emotional skill building, CBT techniques, crisis intervention, de-escalation, and clinical documentation would allow me to contribute positively to your program while supporting the clinical team and maintaining the safety of adolescent clients. I understand the importance of working within the scope of a non-clinical role, communicating concerns appropriately, and collaborating with clinicians when safety or behavioral concerns arise. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my dedication, adaptability, and passion for working with adolescents to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application, and I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience can contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Shadrack JeanBaptiste

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy,
 
I would like to express my interest in the Mental Health Technician position listed on Indeed. This position would equip me with the experience, development, and fine-tuning of skills associated with that of ensuring the mental betterment of teens/adolescents dealing with mental health and behavioral challenges. I want to be a part of Adolescent Wellness Academy’s pursuit of supporting, advocating for, and providing specialized care for teens/adolescents and their families. 

As a senior attending the University of Central Florida, I’ve sought after roles that would help me build a background of experience that’d help me be able to contribute to the line of work that is social services and mental health care, especially for children. This past summer I worked as a camp counselor, though titled Cabin Staff, at a non-profit medical stay-away camp known as Camp Boggy Creek for children, or rather campers, dealing with life-threatening illness. During my time spent as Cabin Staff, I’ve gained experience in working with campers of various ages and illness groups. With being held responsible for my campers as a counselor, I maintained thorough supervision and redirection as to how they participated in and navigated camp. This supervision involved being aware of their physical, medical, and especially their behavioral norms and needs. The day-to-day experience and skill requirement was not simply understanding and tending to their needs, or redirecting behavior, but to foster connections with campers by playing with them and immersing them into camp culture. This required consistently developing and adapting to the way I not only play with my campers, but also how I communicate with them as well. 

For experience related to more technical and desk-associated work, I held the position of Department Director of Staff Training at A Better Way Campaign, Inc. This campaign was founded by those of Resilience, Inc., a company that helped establish and build upon Social Emotional Learning (SEL) tools in school.. This leadership experience has equipped me with skills in management, coordination, auditing, and analytical assessment. I’ve not only relied on, but too, built upon my skills in communication and assessing the needs of departments’ and their leaders when it came to forming the foundations of strong, efficient, and consistent training programs within the campaign. Through my own assessment, I’ve been able to identify and advocate for the needs of training programs on a frequent basis. In the management and auditing of multiple departments, my skills in multi-tasking as well have been proven reliable.
 
I am in great anticipation of being considered by Adolescent Wellness Academy, and to further showcase this interest, I’ve provided my resume through the Indeed application. In this anticipation, I would be thrilled by the opportunity for an interview. If in need of more information regarding my application, I can be contacted at Taylorjd2007@gmail.com, or (954) 336-9939.
 
Thank you, 
Taylor Dent

The camp I worked at is known as Camp Boggy Creek, a medical stay-away camp for children dealing with life threatening illnesses. There I was trained and gained experience in handling not only the medical and physical needs of my campers, but notably their mental/psychological needs. This involved supervising and playing with them for almost every second of their respectable weeks at camp. Under many situations did I have--and did--keep my composure in stressful or escalated situations, whether it be behaviorally or medically. I played with a variety of age groups, and I believe I did especially well with playing with, and too supporting my oldest/adolescent campers. I've also had to establish and ensure proper documentation of incidents, as well as camper behavior. Additionally, I was held responsible as a mandated reporter for my campers where concern regarding their behaviors or conversations that may come to my attention, even if it may be seen as a non-concern until decided otherwise by clinical, qualified behavioral staff. As a counselor, I made sure to work cooperatively alongside my fellow 3 co-counselors to make sure all decisions regarding our campers, both individually and as a cabin, were not built off of my judgement alone.

I am excited about the opportunity to join Adolescent Wellness Academy because of its commitment to providing comprehensive care that empowers young people to heal, grow, and reach their full potential. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to be considered for the Mental Health Specialist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am currently pursuing a B.S. in Behavioral Neuroscience on a pre-med track, and adolescent mental health is not simply an area in which I am seeking work experience; it is the field I hope to dedicate my career to. My long-term goal is to attend medical school and ultimately become a child and adolescent psychiatrist.

My previous experience as a volunteer medical assistant in an outpatient psychiatric practice gave me the opportunity to work within a mental health care environment and interact directly with patients and clinical staff. I assisted with patient intake, documentation and charting, medication-related administrative tasks, insurance forms, and patient communication. Through this experience, I developed a greater understanding of the responsibility that comes with working with individuals receiving psychiatric care, including the importance of compassion, professionalism, confidentiality, careful observation, accurate documentation, and communication with the clinical team.

My interest in mental health began well before college. I have been involved in mental health advocacy for years, including youth-focused advocacy and participation with the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry. These experiences helped solidify my desire to work specifically with young people and eventually pursue child and adolescent psychiatry.

What particularly draws me to this position is the opportunity to be present with adolescents during the everyday moments of treatment. I would truly value the chance to help maintain a safe and supportive environment, building appropriate rapport, providing structure, observing changes or concerns, and supporting the clinical team. I understand that the Mental Health Specialist role is not to independently provide therapy or make clinical decisions, but to be a reliable, emotionally regulated, and attentive member of the treatment team who knows when concerns need to be escalated.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my psychiatric clinical experience, behavioral neuroscience education, commitment to mental health advocacy, and genuine passion for working with adolescents to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am eager to continue learning while contributing to an environment where teenagers feel safe, respected, supported, and understood.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and goals could contribute to your team.

Gratefully,
Scarlett McKeehan

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team, 

My name is Yenifer Padron, I’m a bilingual behavioral health professional in training with direct, hands-on experience supporting at-risk youth in structured and educational settings. Being part of trauma-informed practices, prosocial behavior intervention, and youth program management is what gives me a sense of purpose, which is why I think your role as a Youth Wellness Advocate is the perfect fit for me. 

I grew up as the youngest sibling in a low income household with immigrant parents. Both of my parents suffered many traumatic experiences as children in their home countries which then impacted the way my older sister and I grew up here in the United States. My brain has purposely blocked out many instances of hardship as a way to protect me, but the one thing I clearly remember are the resources my mom sought out in hopes to rebuild our family and heal from the conflicts we faced. Institutions like Adolescent Wellness Academy are what kept my family and I grounded amongst the very rocky years of my sisters adolescence as well as my own. 

For the past three years, I’ve worked with at-risk youth in low income areas, helping them reach educational and developmental milestones while fostering a healthy sense of self worth, confidence, acceptance and motivation. 

I’ve been a first hand witness to the conflicts that arise with youth that are simply a reaction to the many transitions they go through at this age, in combination with conflicts at home, it can easily become very harmful. Although I’ve also been privileged to witness and be part of meaningful deescalations that lead to conflict resolution and lasting positive impact to their psychological development. As an After-School Counselor with Miami Children’s Museum, I provided direct support to at-risk youth on a daily basis, with the goal of nurturing positive reinforcement, structured expectations, and collaborative communication with their families and my colleagues. While the focus was enrichment and academic skill building, at the center was prosocial values with the goal of community building and restoration. As a Youth Wellness Advocate I hope to do just that, advocate for their wellness as well as their families wellness and be part of the reason everyone heals and grows to reach that light at the end of what seems to be a very dark tunnel. 

Thank you for your time and consideration, I would be honored to be part of and learn from Adolescent Wellness Academy and contribute to your mission of supporting and empowering young people. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to your team. 

Sincerely, Yenifer Padron

I possess over 220 hours of supervised clinical practice across four distinct settings: applied clinical care, specialized rehabilitation, school, and community. This uncommon breadth of exposure for a recent graduate has given me an advanced understanding of adolescent developmental needs, enabling me to manage program flow, execute same-day wellness documentation, and support therapeutic schedules with high organizational precision. Furthermore, I conducted 9 individual and family psychotherapy sessions and achieved measurable improvement in patients' treatment goals within a 3-month period, demonstrating my technical readiness to handle front-desk operations, family check-ins, and behavioral tracking.
Supervising teens aged 13–17 during unstructured time and responding to escalated behaviors without engaging in power struggles requires absolute emotional regulation. My previous work at Defensorías Comunitarias in a community deeply affected by violence demonstrates my communication and emotional regulation under high-tension conditions. This specialized trauma-informed resilience allows me to remain calm under pressure, de-escalate crisis situations smoothly, and escalate clinical flags appropriately to primary clinicians. Additionally, my complete English/Spanish bilingualism directly satisfies your core requirement to support South Florida families with professional warmth. My three academic honors—including a Top GPA Award and two consecutive merit scholarships—further certify the intellectual rigor and consistency I bring to this role.
Importantly, as a Chilean citizen, I am fully eligible for the H-1B1 visa under the US-Chile Free Trade Agreement and am prepared to relocate immediately upon hire. This specialized program completely bypasses the traditional H-1B lottery system and features no mandatory government petition fees for the employer. While I am fully prepared to personally cover my own consular application and processing fees at the U.S. Embassy, the onboarding pathway requires minimal institutional action: the employer only needs to file a free Labor Condition Application (LCA) with the Department of Labor and provide a standard job offer letter, making my sponsorship highly streamlined, predictable, and cost-effective for AWA.
Thank you for your time, consideration, and life-changing commitment to adolescent care. I look forward to discussing how my clinical university training, trauma-informed resilience, and bilingual fluency can support your daily program environment.
Sincerely,
Gianella Zambrano Ortega
